title: Rate limit
description: Runtime-neutral TypeScript rate limiting with token bucket, fixed window, and exact sliding window algorithms over a pluggable atomic store, a bounded in-memory LRU store, and Fetch-standard 429 and RateLimit header helpers.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build; the header helpers use the Fetch standard Headers and Response: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers, and Hono handlers on those runtimes.

The included memory store is single-process. Multi-instance, serverless, or edge deployments need an application-supplied shared RateLimitStore (for example Redis or Durable Objects) that honors the atomic update contract.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers, or network activity occur at install or import time.

configuration: createRateLimiter({ algorithm: "token-bucket", limit, refillPerSecond, store, clock?, prefix? }) or ({ algorithm: "fixed-window" | "sliding-window", limit, windowMs, store, clock?, prefix? }). limit 1–1000000 (sliding-window 1–10000).
limiter.consume(key, cost = 1) returns { allowed, limit, remaining, resetAt, resetAfterMs, retryAfterMs }. Denied requests consume nothing.
createMemoryStore({ maxKeys = 10000, clock? }); pass the same clock as the limiter.

Derive keys on the trusted server from an authenticated principal, API key ID, or a client IP taken from your platform's trusted proxy configuration. Never trust a raw X-Forwarded-For header that clients can set.
limitations: The memory store holds state in one JavaScript heap: not shared across processes, workers, isolates, serverless instances, or regions, and lost on restart. LRU eviction under key floods resets evicted keys' quotas.
No Redis, database, or Durable Object store is included; a shared store must implement RateLimitStore atomically and is the application's responsibility to test.
Store errors propagate to the caller; choosing fail-open or fail-closed is the application's decision.
The sliding window keeps one timestamp per allowed unit (exact log), so state grows with limit; limit is capped at 10000 for that algorithm.
Headers use the widely deployed RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset fields (delta seconds); the newer IETF draft RateLimit/RateLimit-Policy structured fields are not emitted.
Key derivation, authentication, and abuse/bot detection are out of scope. Rate limiting is not a DDoS defense on its own.
Tests use an injected clock and the memory store only.
